title: Hardware Interview Prep
description: A guided path through this problem set for interview prep, from warm-up bit tricks through RTL, computer architecture, verification/UVM, analog/mixed-signal modeling, low power, DFT and timing — finishing with live-debugging practice.

stages.title: Warm-Up: Bit Tricks & Combinational Basics
stages.blurb: Quick, no-clock puzzles — the kind of thing an interviewer throws at you in the first five minutes to see how you think about hardware.

stages.title: Sequential Logic & FSMs
stages.blurb: Registers, edge detection, and state machines — the bread-and-butter RTL every interview checks first.

stages.title: Datapath & Arithmetic
stages.blurb: Adders, multipliers, and the arithmetic tricks that come up in nearly every architecture interview.

stages.title: Memories, FIFOs & Buffering
stages.blurb: Classic 'design a FIFO' style questions, from a plain sync RAM up to a full async FIFO with Gray-coded pointers.

stages.title: Clocking & Clock-Domain Crossing
stages.blurb: CDC is one of the most commonly asked digital-design topics — dividers, reset synchronizers, and handshakes.

stages.title: Bus Protocols & Peripherals
stages.blurb: Implement the slave/peripheral side of the buses and serial protocols interviewers love to whiteboard.

stages.title: Arbitration & Flow Control
stages.blurb: Fairness and flow control between multiple requesters — a favorite 'design an arbiter' interview question.

stages.title: Pipelining & Hazards
stages.blurb: Build the pieces of a pipelined CPU datapath and handle the hazards that come with it.

stages.title: Caches & Memory Hierarchy
stages.blurb: Cache structure and replacement policy questions — a computer-architecture interview staple.

stages.title: Advanced Microarchitecture
stages.blurb: Out-of-order execution building blocks and GPU-style scheduling — the harder end of architecture interviews.

stages.title: Verification: Assertions (SVA)
stages.blurb: Write the SystemVerilog assertions a DV engineer is expected to produce on the spot in an interview.

stages.title: Verification: Testbenches & Constrained-Random
stages.blurb: Write testbenches and randomization constraints from scratch — a core DV interview exercise.

stages.title: Verification: UVM
stages.blurb: The UVM component types (driver, monitor, scoreboard, RAL, virtual sequence) that come up in almost every DV interview loop.

stages.title: Analog / Mixed-Signal Modeling
stages.blurb: Behavioral real-number models of the analog building blocks a mixed-signal interview brings up — amplifiers, converters, and filters, expressed as ordinary clocked SystemVerilog/VHDL.

stages.title: Low Power & DFT
stages.blurb: Clock gating, retention, and scan/BIST — the low-power and design-for-test questions ASIC interviews like to probe.

stages.title: Timing Closure
stages.blurb: Redesign a design's logic structure to hit a critical-path budget — a question that separates RTL writers from RTL engineers.

stages.title: Debug Practice: Find the Bug
stages.blurb: Every one of these compiles and looks reasonable at a glance — exactly like the broken RTL an interviewer hands you to debug live.
